# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `tools/fa-clip/` — the native macOS pasteboard helper (gh-2040): a plain
  `NSPasteboard` reader (`fa-clip <png|jpeg|tiff>` → bytes on stdout, exit
  2 = flavor absent), built by `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` into the macOS
  CLI bundles (`bundle/bin/fa-clip`, per-arch) and shipped beside the `fa`
  binary — install.sh, install_local.sh and the self-update swap all copy
  it. The CLI resolves it relative to its own executable, never PATH; a
  missing/broken helper degrades to the named pasteboard-unavailable path.
  NEVER reintroduce the AppleScript/Apple Events clipboard transport
  (`osascript` is grep-gated out of `bin/` + `lib/src/cli/` —
  test/cli/fa_clip_helper_test.dart); the TCC «access data from other
  apps» dialog class must stay dead. macOS text reads stay on `pbpaste`
  (already prompt-free — documented split, gh-2040 AC4).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  gh-1934 (413-proof sessions): image blocks OUTSIDE the kept region —
  first seen before the LAST renumbering boundary — evict to
  `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders (payload-only, JSONL
  byte-identical); kept-region images ride on under the normal caps; the 413 recovery ladder
  (`agent_loop_image_recovery.dart` + `image_recovery.dart`, bounded at
  2 passes per response, each 413 halving the session's adaptive
  `images.maxBytesPerRequest`) drops the oldest images (pass 1), then
  strips ALL images including the current message (pass 2, latched
  session-wide), carrying the `[images] recovered from 413:` notice +
  model-visible note; classification lives in `image_overflow.dart`
  (`isPayloadTooLargeError`), surface wording in `image_drop_ux.dart`
  (`ImageDropReason.evicted`).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape (no eviction, no ladder). `agent_loop.dart` applies it in
  `_buildRequestContext` after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing
  repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  Conformance claims are the self-certification blind spot (gh-1834):
  when the final claim includes parity/conformance to a reference or
  specification (any domain), a "verified" item counts only with
  negative and combination checks — refused incompatible options,
  empty/corrupt inputs, boundary values, must-NOT-work cases — alongside
  happy paths; a blanket "everything matches" is not verified (prompt
  step 2.6, conditional: tasks with no conformance claim are
  unchanged).
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). gh-1835: a foreground bash call still
  running after `waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds` (default 60; 0 = kill
  switch) is auto-backgrounded — CONVERTED, never restarted (it already
  runs as a registry job under the soft-yield path): the pending tool call
  resolves exactly once with the backgrounded result (`bash_auto_background
  .dart` text, anchored on the hand-back sentence so the loop's stuck
  supervisor and budget ladder classify it as a real conversion), the
  settle notification stays armed, an explicit `timeout` at/below the
  threshold keeps the classic path while one above carries over as the
  job's cap, and hosts without `BackgroundShell` keep legacy behavior.
  Headless `fa -p` DRAINS live shell
  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared
  wall-clock ceiling `headless.shellJobDrainMs` (default 30 min; 0 =

  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:

  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`

cube-kernel-live:
    name: Cube kernel live (macOS)
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Content-addressed native-assets hook downloads (sqlite3 et al) are
      # hash-verified on reuse — cache them so a GitHub release-asset
      # brownout (504 bodies hashed as mismatches, 2026-09-21) can't
      # re-break every job that re-downloads.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test cube backends (live kernel legs)
        run: dart test test/cube/backends

      # gh-1059 AC4: the real-keychain runner guard — `security`
      # add/find/delete against the runner's login keychain through the
      # bounded-helper machinery (outcome classification incl. stderr
      # tails, env merge, timeout kill). The group is tagged `integration`
      # (real side effects), so the Linux core shards and the pre-commit
      # gate skip it; this macOS leg is where it actually executes. Skips
      # with a named reason when no `security` binary / default keychain.
      - name: dart test secure key store (macOS Keychain live legs)
        run: dart test test/secrets/secure_key_store_test.dart --tags integration

  static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1538: the publish dry-run below rehearses the tag-stamped
          # stage (gh-1522), moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — tag math needs the full tag graph
          # (blobless per gh-1477, same incantation that leg used).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi

if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.release-provenance.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Probe every landing-page release link
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --landing site/index.html
      - name: Probe the full required asset set
        env:
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --smoke "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-latest
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./site/install.ps1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (sh)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        env:
          FA_INSTALL_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin
        run: sh ./site/install.sh

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Windows)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: '& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Fa\bin\fa.exe" --version'

      - name: Smoke the installed binary (Unix)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -x "${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin/fa" ]; then
            fa_path="${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin/fa"
          else
            fa_path="$HOME/.local/bin/fa"

content.text:
run: flutter build ${{ matrix.os }} --release

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # gh-1659 — the Office add-in acceptance suite folded into the shared
  # matrix. It lived in office-addin.yml under push/pull_request triggers
  # (branches:[main], path-filtered), so every lib/**- or flutter_app/**-
  # touching PR paid for a SECOND standalone workflow whose check had to
  # be tracked separately in branch protection. Path-triggered here
  # exactly like exzone/locksmoke: pull_request events + SM validation
  # dispatches (the merge-base classifier; its fail-safe arm runs it) on
  # the SAME path list the standalone triggers carried. A red suite
  # reddens the required Quality gate (platform class, #1368) — it must
  # block the merge, never the pure-Dart publish. The bare check-run name
  # is UNCHANGED ("Office add-in suite" — rulesets match the job name;
  # only the workflow display prefix becomes "CI / …").
  # office-addin.yml keeps ONLY workflow_dispatch: the daily-publish
  # addin leg still dispatches it directly (#423 dispatch group intact);
  # the two job bodies are pinned step-identical by
  # test/ci_1659_office_addin_matrix_test.dart — update both together.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # Same two-event guard as exzone/locksmoke: pull_request + SM
    # validation dispatches. Tags/schedule/release never ran the suite
    # (the standalone push trigger was branches:[main] only) and skip it.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.office_addin == 'true' &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential-File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run

# Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pin_release.sh — advance the `vpinned` release marker to a freshly signed
# tag. PURE RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION: no commits, no pushes, no
# working-tree mutation — the marker lives entirely in GitHub Releases.
# The tag-scoped install-pin-bump CI job runs this after release-provenance
# published SHA256SUMS(.sig) for the tag.
#
# Trust model (SEC-07 #795): the marker is only a POINTER. Before it moves,
# the target release must pass check_install_pin.sh (signature verifies
# against the committed trust anchor + full platform coverage); after it
# moves, the gate runs again against the marker itself. A compromised
# marker therefore degrades to a DoS (install fails closed), never to a
# bad binary — the installer's embedded anchor is the real trust root.
#
# Usage:
#   pin_release.sh <tag>            point the vpinned marker at <tag> (vX.Y.Z)
#   pin_release.sh is-newer <a> <b> exit 0 iff semver(a) > semver(b)
#                                   (v-prefixes stripped; numeric compare)
#
# Environment:
#   GH_TOKEN             release write token (live mode)
#   PIN_RELEASE_BASE     file:// dir acting as the release root — fixture
#                        mode: the marker becomes $base/vpinned/PINNED_VERSION
#                        and no gh/network is touched (selftest/dry runs)
#   PIN_RELEASE_REPO     owner/repo for gh calls (default: IstiN/flutter_agent_harness)
#   MARKER_TAG           marker release/tag name (default: vpinned)
# POSIX-only below: Ubuntu's /bin/sh is dash — no pipefail, no arrays/[[]].
# Enable pipefail only where the shell supports it (same convention as
# site/install.sh.template).
set -eu
( set -o pipefail ) 2>/dev/null && set -o pipefail || true

MARKER="${MARKER_TAG:-vpinned}"
REPO="${PIN_RELEASE_REPO:-IstiN/flutter_agent_harness}"
BASE="${PIN_RELEASE_BASE:-https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download}"

# ── is-newer <a> <b>: numeric semver compare, v-prefix tolerated ────────────
# POSIX-pure on purpose: ubuntu runners give `sh` = dash and `awk` = mawk,
# whose printf does not apply the %010d zero-padding this compare relies on
# (the old awk ver_key made equal keys and silently reported "not newer").
# Here every component is normalized with the SHELL printf (dash/bash both
# implement %010d) to a zero-padded digit string — pure digits of equal
# length, so the lexical `>` is collation-independent.
if [ "${1:-}" = "is-newer" ]; then
  a="$(printf '%s' "${2:?usage: is-newer <a> <b>}" | sed 's/^v//')"
  b="$(printf '%s' "${3:?usage: is-newer <a> <b>}" | sed 's/^v//')"
  a_num="${a%%-*}"; a_sfx="${a#"$a_num"}"
  b_num="${b%%-*}"; b_sfx="${b#"$b_num"}"
  # leading digits of a dotted component, zero-stripped, padded to 10
  comp10() {
    c="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -cd '0-9' | sed -e 's/^0*//' -e 's/^$/0/')"
    printf '%010d' "$c"
  }
  split3() { # $1 = "X.Y.Z" → newline-separated X, Y, Z (missing pieces empty)
    rest="$1"
    c1="${rest%%.*}"; [ "$c1" = "$rest" ] && rest="" || rest="${rest#*.}"
    c2="${rest%%.*}"; [ "$c2" = "$rest" ] && c3="" || c3="${rest#*.}"
    printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$c1" "$c2" "$c3"
  }
  # sed-extract instead of `set -- $(...)` — word-splitting drops the empty
  # components, and `set -u` then kills $2/$3 in dash.
  a123="$(split3 "$a_num")"
  a1="$(printf '%s\n' "$a123" | sed -n 1p)"
  a2="$(printf '%s\n' "$a123" | sed -n 2p)"
  a3="$(printf '%s\n' "$a123" | sed -n 3p)"
  b123="$(split3 "$b_num")"
  b1="$(printf '%s\n' "$b123" | sed -n 1p)"
  b2="$(printf '%s\n' "$b123" | sed -n 2p)"
  b3="$(printf '%s\n' "$b123" | sed -n 3p)"
  ka="$(comp10 "$a1")$(comp10 "$a2")$(comp10 "$a3")"
  kb="$(comp10 "$b1")$(comp10 "$b2")$(comp10 "$b3")"
  if [ "$ka" != "$kb" ]; then
    [ "$ka" \> "$kb" ]
    exit $?
  fi
  # equal numerics: a release outranks its own pre-release; release vs
  # release is equal (NOT newer)
  if [ -z "$a_sfx" ] && [ -n "$b_sfx" ]; then exit 0; fi
  if [ -n "$a_sfx" ] || [ -z "$b_sfx" ]; then exit 1; fi
  [ "$a_sfx" \> "$b_sfx" ]
  exit $?
fi

tag="${1:?usage: pin_release.sh <vX.Y.Z>}"
case "$tag" in
  v*) version="${tag#v}" ;;
  *)  version="$tag"; tag="v$tag" ;;
esac
echo "pin_release: target $tag (marker: $MARKER)"

# The gate speaks URLs; a bare fixture path gets a file:// scheme. The raw
# path is kept for fixture-mode marker writes.
BASE_URL="$BASE"
case "$BASE_URL" in
  *://*) ;;
  *) BASE_URL="file://$BASE_URL" ;;
esac

fetch_text() {
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then curl -fsSL "$1"; else wget -qO- "$1"; fi
}

# ── 1. read the current marker (absent = first pin) ─────────────────────────
current=""
if current="$(fetch_text "$BASE_URL/$MARKER/PINNED_VERSION" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')"; then
  echo "pin_release: marker currently at $current"
else
  echo "pin_release: no marker yet — first pin"
fi
if [ -n "$current" ] && ! "$0" is-newer "$version" "$current"; then
  echo "pin_release: marker is already at $current (>= $tag) — nothing to do."
  exit 0
fi

# ── 2. the target must pass the provenance gate BEFORE the marker moves ─────
# FA_PIN_TARGET checks the concrete tag regardless of where the marker
# currently points; PATH overrides keep a fixture-mode gate anchored here.
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
FA_PIN_TARGET="$tag" \
FA_PIN_CONFIG="${FA_PIN_CONFIG:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../site/install-config.yaml}" \
FA_PIN_INSTALLER="${FA_PIN_INSTALLER:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../site/install.sh}" \
FA_PIN_RELEASE_BASE="$BASE_URL" \
  bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/check_install_pin.sh" \
  || { echo "::error::pin_release: $tag failed the provenance gate — marker NOT moved"; exit 1; }

# ── 3. publish the marker ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# NB: gh names the uploaded asset after the FILE basename — the file must
# literally be called PINNED_VERSION inside a temp dir.
tmp_dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pin_marker.XXXXXX")"
printf '%s\n' "$tag" > "$tmp_dir/PINNED_VERSION"
if [ -n "${PIN_RELEASE_BASE:-}" ]; then
  # Fixture mode: write the marker file directly into the release root.
  mkdir -p "$BASE/$MARKER"
  cp "$tmp_dir/PINNED_VERSION" "$BASE/$MARKER/PINNED_VERSION"
  echo "pin_release: fixture marker written: $BASE/$MARKER/PINNED_VERSION"
else
  if ! gh release view "$MARKER" --repo "$REPO" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "pin_release: creating marker release $MARKER"
    gh release create "$MARKER" --repo "$REPO" \
      --title "Pinned known-good release" \
      --notes "Pointer release: the PINNED_VERSION asset names the current known-good Fa release. Advanced only by the install-pin-bump CI job after signed provenance (SEC-07 #795). The marker itself is untrusted — installers verify the pointed release's SHA256SUMS.sig against the committed trust anchor."
  fi
  gh release upload "$MARKER" "$tmp_dir/PINNED_VERSION" --repo "$REPO" --clobber
  echo "pin_release: marker uploaded: $MARKER -> $tag"
fi
rm -rf "$tmp_dir"

# ── 4. post-publish: the marker itself must now verify end-to-end ───────────
retried=false
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  if FA_PIN_CONFIG="${FA_PIN_CONFIG:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../site/install-config.yaml}" \
     FA_PIN_INSTALLER="${FA_PIN_INSTALLER:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../site/install.sh}" \
     FA_PIN_RELEASE_BASE="$BASE_URL" \
     bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/check_install_pin.sh"; then
    retried=true
    break
  fi
  echo "pin_release: post-publish gate attempt $attempt failed — retrying in 10s (asset propagation?)"
  sleep 10
done
$retried || { echo "::error::pin_release: marker does not verify after publish"; exit 1; }

echo ""
echo "pin_release: marker $MARKER now points at $tag (provenance-verified)"

---
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- feat(gh-2059): browser-extension compaction parity with CLI — over-window
  relief, `/compact` with visible receipts, and the shared under-window
  guarantee ride the same `CompactionHostWiring` resolution as the CLI and
  app (`resolveExtensionCompactionWiring`); receipts are durable across
  panel attach/SW restart. Machine-review round 1: exact ladder pass
  counts, busy-matrix routing (`routeUserInput`) for panel text and second
  `/compact` during a pass, window settings from the ACTIVE stored source
  with positive validation, string-encoded int merges.

- fix(gh-2055): the daily-publish `cli` leg red-failed in `pod install`
  (Build macOS x86_64, run 41778615815) because the vendored macOS pod's
  XCFramework download block guarded on the downloaded-zip MARKER
  (`if [ ! -f wasm_run-v0.1.0.zip ]`) instead of on the artifact the build
  consumes. A fresh CI clone never has the marker, so pod install re-ran
  the block on every build: it removed the WasmRun.xcframework the
  build-macos.yml restore step had already placed (cache hit,
  sha256-verified), re-downloaded the 92.7 MB asset with a bare
  no-`--fail` curl, and one transient reset (curl 56 at ~3 MB/92.7 MB)
  left the Podfile `nm -gU` symbol check with no
  macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a to read. The guard now keys on
  `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` — the exact
  path the Podfile force_loads and nm-checks — so the block is a no-op
  whenever the restore step (or a previous run) put the framework in
  place, and the fallback download for a truly cold tree carries
  `--fail` AND aborts the block at the curl step on failure
  (`|| { echo "wasm_run download failed" >&2; exit 1; }` — a swallowed
  status fell through to unzip/truncate residue and masked the root cause
  behind the Podfile `nm` diagnostic; review round 1 on this PR), and the
  podspec now assigns the backtick result and raises "wasm_run framework
  fetch failed" unless `$?.success?` — Ruby ignores a bare backtick's
  exit status, so pod install would otherwise have sailed past the failed
  fetch to the downstream `nm` diagnostic (review round 2). Linted
  behaviorally (stubbed curl, no network; POSIX-gated sandbox, plus a
  ruby evaluation of the real fetch statement) by
  test/wasmrun_macos_podspec_download_guard_test.dart.

- fix(gh-2050): the daily-publish `cli` leg red-failed daily when its
  macOS attach arrived after a sibling train had already PUBLISHED the
  derived tag (the same-tag convergence race: mobile leg drafts + the tag
  train publishes ~25 min after dispatch while the serialized self-hosted
  mac builds need ~66 min — v1.0.685: draft 05:22:46, published 05:44:52,
  mac leg attached 06:28:53). `scripts/release_asset_gate.sh` gains a
  caller-declared pre-stage policy — `RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1` —
  that turns the PUBLISHED+unattached-fa-* verdict into a loud whole-call

gh-2065 [ci-red] v1.0.693 failed
Closes #2065
### Root Cause
`Hostile ambient env` went red on one load-sensitive test — `test/hub/local_hub_relay_concurrency_test.dart` "AC2 paced: an over-cap upload is cut off at the cap …" — with an unhandled `SocketException: Connection reset by peer`. The test deliberately exercises the close-only 413 path (issue #794): the hub destroys the client socket mid-upload, and the test's `Timer.periodic` pump keeps writing chunks into the dead socket. dart:io reports that write-side failure on `socket.done` (`Socket` is `Stream` **and** `IOSink`; the test only handled the read side) → unhandled async error → red test. Pure scheduling: the same test passed in `Core tests (shard 3/4)` of the same run. `Quality gate` (`a leg is failure (hostile-env)`) and downstream `Advance vpinned marker` (publish legs skipped on the red gate → no `SHA256SUMS`; `pin_release.sh` correctly refused) failed only as consequences.

### Fix
- `test/hub/local_hub_relay_concurrency_test.dart` (AC2 paced): swallow the write-side echo — `unawaited(socket.done.then(...))`; the RST is the by-design outcome here, its write-side report is noise.
- Same file: new deterministic twin `REG gh-2065: a pump tick landing after the close-only 413 RST must not leak a write-side socket error` — forces the post-RST pump tick that CI load hit (100 ms grace past the RST before cancelling the pump), so the leak can never silently return.

### Test Coverage
- REG test verified RED pre-fix (`SocketException: Broken pipe (OS Error: Broken pipe, errno = 32)` — same write-side channel as CI's errno 104), GREEN post-fix.
- `dart test test/hub/local_hub_relay_concurrency_test.dart`: 10/10; re-run 10× under CPU load: 0 failures.
- Full hostile-env suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration` + the exact `FA_*`/`FAH_*` env block from the CI job): 13461 passed, 1 failed — see Notes; the ticket's failing test and all 10 relay tests passed inside it.

### Notes
- No product-code change: the close-only answer is the documented issue-#794 design; the defect was the fixture not consuming its socket's write-side error channel.
- The 1 local failure (`test/hub/dap_resume_membership_test.dart`, `TimeoutException after 0:00:05`) is a sandbox-slowness artifact, NOT a regression: it passes in this CI run's Hostile ambient env job and in all Core shards, passes 3/3 in isolation here, and passes 3/3 run together with the relay file; this 4-core sandbox runs the suite ~4× slower than CI (≈44 min vs 11m48s), blowing that test's 5s budget. Left untouched (green in CI, owned by test-automation) — flagging for visibility.

    name: Release pending check (gh-1551)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:

    steps:

      # gh-1477 (commit metadata only — the exact incantation the static
      # stamp rehearsal uses). Schedule events only: every other arm
      # short-circuits in the script and must not pay the fetch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          pending=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ]; then
            # Same semver-tag selection as the static stamp rehearsal
            # below. A schedule checkout IS main's tip (the default
            # branch), so HEAD is exactly "origin/main HEAD" for the
            # comparison the ticket asks for.
            latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
              echo "::warning::no semver v* tag found — treating the tick as release-pending (first-release arm)"
            else
              head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
              new_commits=$(git rev-list --count "$latest"..HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo -1)
              echo "latest tag: $latest"
              echo "main HEAD:  $head_sha"
              echo "commits on main since tag: $new_commits"
              if [ "$new_commits" -eq 0 ]; then
                echo "::notice::empty schedule tick — nothing landed on main since $latest; the quality gate and release short-circuit (gh-1551)"
                pending=false
              elif [ "$new_commits" -lt 0 ]; then
                echo "::warning::git rev-list against $latest failed — fail-open, running the full gate"
              fi
            fi
          else
            echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — the pending check never blocks tag pushes, release events or dispatch arms (gh-1551)"

      # INLINE (not a composite action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...`

      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"

            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true

          fi

No test pins the cube-kernel-live timeout or checkout. Good — I have freedom to change the job's checkout approach and ceiling.

Now let me decide the fix precisely. Let me re-verify the facts once more:

**v1.0.695 run 42511425580, Cube kernel live (macOS):**
- Set up job: 18:45:09 → 18:45:34 (25s — the box was slow even here; hosted runners do this in ~2s, but self-hosted "Set up job" includes runner registration... 25s is slow-ish)
- Checkout: 18:45:34 → 18:55:06 (9m32s, CANCELED — never finished)
- Job ceiling: timeout-minutes: 10 (started 18:45:06 → cancelled 18:55:22)

**v1.0.694 run 42496815925, same job:**
- Set up job: 15:51:48 → 15:52:07 (19s)
- Checkout: 15:52:07 → 15:52:12 (5s)
- Full job: 1m12s.

So checkout went 5s → 9.5min-canceled. Classic transient network stall on github.com from the box (or CPU starvation making git appear hung). The job ceiling then turned "slow" into "red".

The two compounding repo defects:
1. **No stall tolerance in the checkout** — plain github.com actions/checkout, the only self-hosted m5 job not using the hardened mirror-checkout pattern (gh-160 AC2 / gh-164 / gh-1665 lineage in build-macos.yml + build-mobile.yml "the three mirror-checkout jobs").

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The clone lands in a SIBLING
#     dir ("$mirror.recreate") and is swapped in ONLY on success — a
#     recreate whose every attempt dies mid-transfer leaves the last
#     good (stale-but-valid) mirror in place instead of nothing at all
#     (gh-1665 review thread 3; the dependent checkouts pull tip blobs
#     from origin anyway). The partial dir is removed before EVERY
#     attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that would fail the
#     next attempt with "already exists"), and the recreation is a
#     BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial clone dir behind ("$mirror.recreate" is always
#     cleaned up); the previous mirror survives a failed recreate.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout (see build-ios) — the bare
      # workspace rm -rf must never fail this checkout on stale unremovable
      # leftovers in the persistent shared workspace. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box that is the PREVIOUS
      # run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi

          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

4441:  release-provenance:
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg

    # aggregate through the platform-leg verdict (anything not
    # success/skipped is red, #1368) and killing the release train
    # downstream. 30 min clears that stall with ~20 min of slack and sits
    # at the sibling hosted-macos build leg class (build-ios: 30); a
    # genuinely wedged box is still killed loudly, just later. Pinned by
    # test/ci_cube_kernel_ceiling_guard_test.dart.
    timeout-minutes: 30

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Content-addressed native-assets hook downloads (sqlite3 et al) are
      # hash-verified on reuse — cache them so a GitHub release-asset
      # brownout (504 bodies hashed as mismatches, 2026-09-21) can't
      # re-break every job that re-downloads.

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2070 [ci-red] v1.0.695 failed

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The v1.0.695 release run (42511425580, tag push, HEAD b7fc248) went
red: the required `Quality gate` aggregate job failed, blocking the release
train.

**Root cause**: `Cube kernel live (macOS)` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job
`cube-kernel-live`) was killed by its own job-level `timeout-minutes: 10`
while its FIRST step — a plain github.com `actions/checkout` — was still
running. The checkout started 18:45:34 and was cancelled at 18:55:06
(9m32s, never completed); the job died `cancelled` at its 10-minute ceiling
(18:55:22). Baseline on the same box: checkout takes 1–3 s (8 observed
runs, full-job walls 68–114 s; e.g. run 42496815925 checkout = 5 s). The
stall is the documented fa-m5 contention class (gh-2013: the pool is ONE
host under ONE user account with fa-m5 / fa-m5-2 / fa-m5-3 registrations;
"each build crawls ~10x its solo time"), and 10 min was the tightest
ceiling on the box, sized to the healthy wall.

The aggregate reds because `cube-kernel-live` is a platform leg (#1368):
`if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]` → `platform_red=true`
→ `Quality gate FAILED: a platform/native leg is red`. A `cancelled` leg
is deliberately never a pass.

**Impact**: Release-blocking required check red on the v1.0.695 ref.
Consequences, all downstream of the one cancelled leg:
- `Auto-release (tag cut)` skipped (needs quality-gate success).
- `release-provenance` ("Sign release checksums") skipped (needs
  `binaries`, itself skipped behind the gate) → no SHA256SUMS(.sig)
  published for the tag.
- `Advance vpinned marker` failed loudly BY DESIGN: `install-pin-bump`
  runs under `always()`, `scripts/pin_release.sh` re-verifies provenance
  before moving the marker (`check_install_pin.sh` with FA_PIN_TARGET),
  found no provenance and refused — the fail-loud contract from the
  install-pin-bump comment block (the gh-2065 run showed the identical
  consequence shape). The pub.dev publish itself was NOT affected
  (dart_ok stays true on platform-only red, #1368; "Publish to pub.dev"
  succeeded 19:03–19:06).

**Fix approach**: Structural, same class as gh-1778 (test-core budget
killed mid-green-run on v1.0.621): raise the leg ceiling 10 → 30 minutes —
clears the observed 9m32s stall with ~20 min of slack, sits at the sibling
hosted-macos build leg class (`build-ios`: 30), and keeps fail-loud
semantics (a genuinely wedged box is still killed, just later). Pinned by
a new YAML-level guard test `test/ci_cube_kernel_ceiling_guard_test.dart`
(AC1 ceiling ≥ 30; AC2 the leg stays routed to the shared `macos-m5` pool;
AC3 no step-level `timeout-minutes` reintroduces a gh-2070-magnitude kill
under the job ceiling). No product code is involved — the cube/keychain
tests themselves were green in every observed run.

**Previous attempt**: none — first return of this ticket.

content.text: 5cc6890 gh-2070 [ci-red] v1.0.695 failed: cube-kernel-live ceiling 10 -> 30

## gh-2070 — fixed

**What failed:** the v1.0.695 release run (42511425580) reddened the required `Quality gate` — but no leg actually failed. `Cube kernel live (macOS)` was killed **by its own `timeout-minutes: 10`** while its first step (plain github.com `actions/checkout`) was still stalled: 9m32s against a 1–3 s baseline (8 observed runs: full-job walls 68–114 s). The job concluded `cancelled`; the platform-leg verdict reds on anything not success/skipped (#1368). Everything else was downstream: `Auto-release` skipped, provenance never signed, and `Advance vpinned marker` refused to move the marker **by design** (`pin_release.sh` fail-closed without signed SHA256SUMS — the same consequence shape as the gh-2065/v1.0.693 precedent). The pub.dev publish was unaffected (dart_ok stays true on platform-only red).

**Fix (structural, gh-1778 precedent):** `cube-kernel-live` ceiling 10 → 30 minutes (sibling hosted-macos `build-ios` class; ~20 min of slack over the observed stall; a genuinely wedged box still fails loudly), plus a YAML-level guard test pinning AC1 ceiling ≥ 30, AC2 `macos-m5` routing, AC3 no step-level timeout reintroducing the kill. Verified RED pre-fix (AC1: expected ≥ 30, actual 10), GREEN post-fix; 315 workflow-shape/unit tests across all `ci.yml`-parsing guard files pass; change committed to `ai/gh-2070` on top of the dev base.

Adjacent gaps documented in `outputs/rca.md`, deliberately not fixed (minimum-fix discipline): the degraded-runner watchdog is `pull_request`-only and its detector misses `cancelled`-conclusion (timeout) jobs; the mirror-checkout hardening used by the other self-hosted legs needs new tag/PR-merge-ref handling to port here.
